raw_response:
I will keep my land in the standard Quzhou pattern of winter wheat followed by summer maize. In my county, that rotation fits the climate, the machinery, and the market best. Rainfall is concentrated in summer, so maize matches the rainy season well, while wheat can still produce reliably if I irrigate at key stages. I am 60 and well educated, so I will not chase a complicated mix of crops that raises management risk. I would rather run one clean, efficient grain system, use better seed, return straw to the field, and manage fertilizer more precisely. For wheat, I will use an improved high-yield variety, prepare a good seedbed with rotary tillage, apply balanced N-P-K with most phosphorus and potassium as base fertilizer, split nitrogen between base and topdressing, irrigate at the most important growth stages, and keep disease control timely but not excessive. After wheat harvest, I will direct-seed hybrid summer maize quickly to protect the growing season, keep tillage to no-tillage to save time and moisture, rely mostly on summer rain with only limited supplemental irrigation, and control weeds, borers, and foliar disease as needed. My goal is steady grain output, controlled input cost, and protection of soil and water rather than pushing for the absolute maximum yield.
